symbolic_operation: Logical deduction over weighted cross-KG rules; symbolic inference engine; explainer based on rule paths.
final_decision_by: Unified neuro-symbolic probabilistic model: rule-regularised MRF optimised by variational EM, then joint symbolic/neural inference of the alignments.
evidence_quote: “After training, the missing alignments are jointly inferred by both components.” “NeuSymEA unifies them under a joint probability objective.” The explainer generates supporting rule-path pairs with confidence scores.

symbolic_operation: Fuzzy inference system with recursive entity and relation alignment rules, fixed-point iteration and t-norms.
final_decision_by: The fuzzy system computes the scores and the alignment; language models only provide fixed literal similarities.
evidence_quote: This is very different from our approach, where Fuzzy Logic is central in the alignment process, for both entities and relations. After initialization, the steps of entity alignment (Equation 1) and subrelation alignment (Equation 2) are applied alternately.

symbolic_operation: PARIS probabilistic reasoning module, enriched by semantic embeddings and iterated until the final mappings.
final_decision_by: The PR module initialises and infers logically consistent mappings with the help of the SE module and produces the final output.
evidence_quote: Highly confident PR mappings are selected as alignment seeds for SE training; after each iteration the SE outputs are fed back to PR, and “the PR module finally outputs the entity mappings.”

symbolic_operation: Non-Axiomatic Logic (NAL) inference over Type I/II/III paths, evidence aggregation and revision.
final_decision_by: A separate NAL engine produces the conclusions and the alignment; BERT provides scores or premises.
evidence_quote: In this paper, we introduce NALA, an entity alignment method that captures three types of logical inference paths with Non-Axiomatic Logic (NAL). Type I&II align the entity pairs and type III aligns relations. NALA iteratively aligns entities and relations by integrating the conclusions of the inference paths.

symbolic_operation: Class conflict matrix derived from disjointness and hierarchy, with conflict and membership losses in the joint embedding.
final_decision_by: Mappings are predicted by similarity of the learned embeddings; the constraints acted during training.
evidence_quote: we propose an ontology-guided entity alignment method named OntoEA, where both KGs and their ontologies are jointly embedded, and the class hierarchy and the class disjointness are utilized to avoid false mappings.

symbolic_operation: AMIE+ and ontology rules turned into grounded rules and injected into the training objective (hybrid loss).
final_decision_by: Embeddings score the candidates; symbolic rules constrain the representation learning.
evidence_quote: Grounding rules refer to the replacement of variables that are contained in the rules with concrete entities. For example, the rule “manager < ?a, ?b > ⇒ superior < ?a, ?b > ” can be converted to the rule “manager < Lisa, Amy > ⇒ superior < Lisa, Amy > ” after the transformation.

symbolic_operation: HermiT infers implicit contexts and hierarchy before verbalisation and embedding; type constraints reduce false positives.
final_decision_by: Transformer embeddings, cosine similarity, the Hungarian algorithm and thresholding produce the mappings.
evidence_quote: “We use the HermiT reasoner to infer logical axioms and sub-class hierarchy.” “The Hungarian algorithm is used to enforce optimal one-to-one alignment.” “Finally, we enforce domain constraints to remove inconsistent pairs.”
evidence_section: Embedding-based alignment architecture; Ontology preprocessing; Thresholding and filtering

symbolic_operation: Knowledge-based rules over UMLS CUIs, hierarchy, attribute alignment and an integration/judgment step.
final_decision_by: BERT handles sentence-type phenotype units, the knowledge-based method handles logic-type units, and the integration/judgment step classifies similarity.
evidence_quote: Speciﬁcally, em- ploying a BERT-based pre-trained language model (PLMs) to align phrase-type PhenoSSUs and a knowledge-based method for logic-type PhenoSSUs demonstrates efﬁcacy. Moreover, by successfully integrating the PhenoSSU align- ment and extraction algorithms, we have developed Phe- noAlign.

symbolic_operation: Rule mining, grounding, backward reasoning and propagation filter augmented triples before KG embedding.
final_decision_by: MTransE/AlignE/AliNet produce the alignment; the rules augment and filter triples upstream.
evidence_quote: The mined rules and rule groundings are human-understandable, and can make the augmentation procedure reliable. The inference of entity alignment is based on the distances between entity embeddings.

symbolic_operation: Probabilistic reasoning (label refiner) minimises the structural incompatibility of LLM pseudo-labels before training the base EA model.
final_decision_by: The base EA model produces the alignment; probabilistic reasoning filters the pseudo-labels upstream.
evidence_quote: LLM4EA incorporates an unsupervised label refiner that enhances label accuracy by selecting a subset of confident pseudo-labels through probabilistic reasoning. The refinement process is framed as a combinatorial optimization problem aimed at minimizing overall structural incompatibility among labels.

symbolic_operation: Type-constrained preliminary alignment and relation completion generate new relations before GCN embedding.
final_decision_by: GCN and LS-SVM multi-view embeddings produce the final entity alignment; KG completion acts upstream.
evidence_quote: This framework utilizes similarity interaction and entity type constraints for an initial entity alignment, supplemented by logical rules for completing the knowledge graph. Relation Completion. We deem entities ei and ej as preliminarily aligned when sim(e1i, e2i) > α and both entities share the same type.

symbolic_operation: AMIE+ rules mined and transferred across KGs, grounded for KG completion and enforced by a rule-constraint loss.
final_decision_by: Multi-channel GNN/hyperbolic embeddings produce the cross-lingual alignment after rule-guided completion and loss.
evidence_quote: HSMGNN performs KG completion through rule-based reasoning. It employs the AMIE+ rule mining system to extract logical rules from each KG, and transfers them across graphs based on seed-aligned relations. We incorporate grounded rules and introduce a rule constraint loss to ensure that these rules are respected in the manifold embedding space.

symbolic_operation: Root-phrase matching, class-hierarchy propagation, sibling propagation, named-entity typing, WordNet cues and resolution rules build high-confidence CaLiGraph-DBpedia pairs used for distant supervision.
final_decision_by: BERT is fine-tuned on the pairs generated upstream and returns the final probability distribution over DBpedia classes.
evidence_quote: “Our method consists of two main parts: (1) Generating distantly-supervised training samples. (2) Finetuning pretrained language models.” “We regard such CaLiGraph-DBpedia pairs as having high confidence, and use these pairs for distant supervision.” “The final output is the probability distribution over the DBpedia classes for the given CaLiGraph class.”
evidence_section: §4.1 Model architecture; §§4.2–4.6 training-pair generation; §4.7 BERT Finetuning

symbolic_operation: Symbolic post-processing: hierarchical mapping extension and logical repair of incoherent mappings.
final_decision_by: BERT predicts and scores mappings; logical extension and repair refine the final mapping.
evidence_quote: Mapping extension iterates until no new mapping is found. Mapping repair then removes mappings leading to logical conflicts; a diagnosis removes a minimal number to restore coherence.

symbolic_operation: subClassOf relations drive positive/negative sampling and SGAT training; final selection by distances and stable marriage.
final_decision_by: Neural embeddings and an improved stable-marriage step select the alignments; the symbolic structure acts upstream.
evidence_quote: We propose a novel inter-intra negative sampling skill tailored for the structural relations asserted in ontologies, and further improve our iterative ﬁnal alignment method by introducing an automatic adjustment of the ﬁnal alignment threshold.

symbolic_operation: OWL/RDFS reasoning enriches axioms and metadata before matching with HGAT/BioBERT.
final_decision_by: Ontology enrichment feeds hyperbolic graph attention networks; matching comes from the learned representations.
evidence_quote: First, we propose an effective ontology-enriching method that reﬁnes and enriches the ontologies through axioms and external resources. Subsequently, we use hyperbolic graph attention layers to encode hierarchical concepts in a uniﬁed hyperbolic space.

symbolic_operation: OWL API and HermiT extract parent, child, equivalent, disjoint and restriction information before recursive neural learning.
final_decision_by: A recursive neural network and cosine similarity produce the alignments; HermiT provides meta-information upstream.
evidence_quote: For parsing the source ontology, we have used a Java API named OWL API and HermiT Reasoner to extract meta information of a class, such as IRI of the class, label of the class, restriction of the class, parent, child, equivalent, and disjoint classes of each class/concept of the ontology.

symbolic_operation: FCA concept lattices and formal contexts refine the embeddings and generate positive/negative pairs; some exact extents become alignments.
final_decision_by: Embeddings refined by the FCA loss and stable marriage produce the alignments; the symbolic part mainly acts in learning.
evidence_quote: Formal contexts generate positive/negative training pairs and refine entity vectors; exact two-entity extents can be treated as alignments, while stable marriage and a threshold produce the matching results.

symbolic_operation: FCA formal contexts and lattices generate training examples and structurally validate the final mappings.
final_decision_by: Siamese BERT produces matches; the structural formal context/lattice validates the final mappings.
evidence_quote: The lexical formal context yields positive training samples; Siamese BERT and stable marriage propose matches; “those validated by the derived structural lattice are the final mappings.”

symbolic_operation: LogMap/AML seed mappings, disjointness constraints checked by a reasoner, and subsumption-based filtering of predicted mappings.
final_decision_by: The Siamese network predicts mappings; symbolic filters remove disjointness/subsumption violations; final output as an ensemble.
evidence_quote: Disjointness constraints filter LogMap anchors to produce training seeds; after SiamNN prediction, disjointness and subsumption checks filter Mp, and the remaining M′p is merged with seeds for the final output.

symbolic_operation: LogMap selects mappings, preserves logical coherence and isolates uncertain mappings; the LLM oracle only handles those uncertain mappings.
final_decision_by: LogMap assembles the alignment and, in the tested variant, replaces its automatic decisions on uncertain mappings with the LLM oracle's answers.
evidence_quote: During mapping selection, LogMap identifies uncertain mappings Mask; without an Oracle it decides automatically. The appendix describes LogMap as combining logical reasoning while preserving consistency.

symbolic_operation: Description-logic reasoning (Pellet), R-MIPS/R-MUPS and kernel revision with incision functions; the language model ranks candidate axioms.
final_decision_by: The revision algorithm removes the selected axioms to restore ontology coherence.
evidence_quote: To resolve the incoherence in a rebuttal ontology K w.r.t. a reliable ontology K0 by removing some axioms from K, a nat- ural way is to remove at least one axiom from each R-MIPS. Removing all axioms in a diagnosis from an ontology will regain coherence of the ontology.

symbolic_operation: Iterative discrete graph search at inference: forward/backward 1-hop SPARQL retrieval, deterministic metadata-relation filtering, entity propagation, beam-state maintenance and path pruning.
final_decision_by: Graph exploration constructs and prunes the evidence paths; the LLM scores relations and entities, assesses sufficiency and derives the final schema pair.
evidence_quote: “We query both forward ... and backward ... relations.” “We apply heuristic filtering.” “We propagate to the next hop’s candidate entities by traversing the selected promising relations.” “The final path score is defined as S_path = S_rel × S_ent.” “Based on this explicit evidence, the LLM derives the final schema matching pair.”
evidence_section: Figure 1; Graph Exploration via SMoG; Iterative Exploration Process

symbolic_operation: CSP-style constraint reasoning with filtering, propagation, closure enforcement, backtracking and fixpoint.
final_decision_by: LLM evidence provides priors; the CSP engine returns the first assignment (fixpoint) compatible with the constraints.
evidence_quote: The LLM does not finalize matches; E provides priors for global reasoning. Constraint filtering removes candidate pairs that violate hard rules. Propagation uses evidence and constraints to iteratively assign matches. The output F* is the first fixpoint assignment that satisfies C.

symbolic_operation: Ontology/KG queries, anchor pairs and hierarchical reasoning injected into the loss of the transformer encoders.
final_decision_by: Embeddings trained with anchor and hierarchy losses are used for semantic annotation and alignment to ontology relations and types.
evidence_quote: We show that by combining the power of symbolic reasoning, neural embeddings, and loss function design, a significant performance improvement can be achieved. Extensive experimentation has shown that explicitly adding the hierarchical reasoning information from the ontology to the training loss makes a significant improvement in the quality of learned embeddings.

symbolic_operation: Matching rules (MRLs) with embedded ML predicates; recursive and collective chase until the fixpoint.
final_decision_by: The chase applies the MRLs until the set of matches cannot be extended; that set is the deduced correspondences.
evidence_quote: “We define MRLs φ over R as X→l.” “The process proceeds until Γ cannot be further extended.” “X provides a logic ‘explanation’ of ML predictions.”
evidence_section: §II Embedding ML Models in Rules; §III Fixpoint Model

symbolic_operation: Embedding-based sampling reduces the KGs; Linkex extracts link keys as symbolic rules that explain and regenerate identity links.
final_decision_by: Embedding methods generate the identity links; Linkex extracts link keys that explain and can regenerate them.
evidence_quote: embedding-based EM approaches are used to sample the KGs... rules (in the form of link keys) are extracted to explain the generation of identity links... link keys can improve the explainability ... allowing for the regeneration of identity links.
